PAGE SEO AUDIT · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

Audit one page's SEO and AI-readiness in ten seconds

Paste the page's HTML (View source, copy all). You get a score, the mistakes ranked by how much they matter, and the exact fix for each: title and description length, headings, canonical, link previews, structured data that actually parses, image alt text, and whether the text exists before JavaScript runs.

Nothing is uploaded. What you paste is read in this browser and never leaves your device, and this page makes no network calls.

1. Paste the page source

Paste HTML above and click Audit.

Result

Run it in CI instead

Zero dependencies, Node 18+. It fetches a URL or reads a file; nothing else.

node cli.mjs audit https://example.com/
node cli.mjs audit dist/index.html --min-score 85

--min-score exits 1 below the score, so a deploy can refuse to ship a page that lost its title or canonical.

Questions people actually ask

What does a free on-page SEO audit check?

Title and meta description length, a single h1 and a sane heading outline, a canonical link, the viewport tag, Open Graph link-preview tags, JSON-LD structured data that actually parses, image alt text, vague link text and how much real text is in the served HTML.

How do I audit a page without uploading it anywhere?

Open the page, choose View source, copy everything and paste it here. The audit runs in your browser and the page makes no network calls. The command-line version fetches a URL or reads a file on your own machine.

What is AI-readiness here?

Six signals AI assistants and answer engines rely on when they read a page: not blocked by noindex, structured data present, enough text in the raw HTML, a description, one clear h1 and a canonical URL. It is a checklist of markup, not a promise of being cited.

Does a score of 100 mean I will rank?

No. Ranking depends on content quality, links, speed and competition, none of which can be seen from one page's markup. This is not an SEO guarantee; it finds the mechanical mistakes that quietly hold a page back.

Why does it ask for pasted HTML instead of a URL?

Browsers block a web page from reading another site's HTML. Pasting the source keeps the tool private and serverless. For URLs, the Node command-line version fetches the page directly and can fail a build below a minimum score.

Longer version: the on-page SEO checklist behind each finding.

seo-checklist-for-a-single-page.html.text:
Page SEO Audit · guide

On-page SEO checklist for a single page

These are the checks Page SEO Audit runs, in order of how much a miss costs. All of them are visible in the page source; none needs a paid tool.

Things that can remove you from results

noindex

A <meta name="robots" content="noindex"> left over from staging tells engines to drop the page. Check it first on any page that is not appearing.

Structured data that does not parse

A trailing comma in JSON-LD makes the whole block invisible. Engines do not warn you; they skip it. Validate the JSON before you publish.

Text that only exists after JavaScript

Many crawlers and most AI assistants read the raw HTML. If the served document is an empty <div id="app">, they see an empty page. Server-render or pre-render the main content.

Things that shape how you look in results

Title (about 30–60 characters)

The headline of your result. Lead with what the page is, then the brand. Every page gets its own.

Meta description (about 70–160 characters)

Not a ranking factor, but it is the sales copy under the title and is often used as the snippet.

One h1 and an orderly outline

Headings are the table of contents that screen readers, engines and AI summarisers navigate by. Do not skip levels.

Canonical link

States the one preferred URL, so ?utm_source= variants and www/non-www copies do not split signals. Make it absolute.

Open Graph tags

og:title, og:description and og:image decide the card shown when someone shares the page in chat or social feeds, which is free distribution you control.

Things that help machines and people

JSON-LD

Match the type to the page: SoftwareApplication, Product, Article, FAQPage, Organization. If the page has visible question-and-answer pairs, mark them up as FAQPage with the same text.

Image alt text, descriptive link text, viewport, lang

Alt text feeds image search and accessibility; "click here" tells a crawler nothing about the target; the viewport tag is the mobile-friendly baseline; lang helps translation and screen readers.

Limits: markup only. Speed, backlinks, content quality and competition are outside what a single page's source can show, so a perfect score is not a ranking promise.
